name: Hanoi
operatingHours: Hanoi Metro Line 2A (Cát Linh–Hà Đông) and Line 3 (Nhổn–Cầu Giấy, elevated section only) both run daily 5:30 AM–10:00 PM; trains every 6 min at weekday peaks, 10 min off-peak and weekends, 15 min after 7:30 PM. The Line 3 underground extension to Hanoi Station is not expected before late 2027. The metro does not reach the Old Quarter; city buses and ride-hailing (Grab, Xanh SM) fill the gaps.
fareInfo: Distance-based single fares (since 1 Aug 2025): Line 2A VND 9,000–19,000, Line 3 VND 9,000–15,000, bought at station machines or by contactless bank card at the gates. Weekly pass VND 160,000, monthly VND 280,000. Free for over-60s and children under 6. City buses ~VND 8,000–10,000.

sights.name: Old Quarter
sights.note: A dense grid of narrow 'tube houses' and guild streets north of Hoàn Kiếm Lake, best explored on foot for street food, temples and scooter-choked lanes.
sights.hours: Open 24 hours; liveliest early morning and evening

sights.name: Hoa Lo Prison
sights.note: The surviving gatehouse and cell blocks of the French colonial jail later nicknamed the 'Hanoi Hilton', telling the story of Vietnamese political prisoners and captured US pilots.
sights.hours: ~8:00 AM–5:00 PM daily; night tours on selected evenings

sights.name: Temple of Literature
sights.note: An 11th-century Confucian temple and Vietnam's first university, a sequence of walled courtyards with stone stelae on tortoises honouring old exam laureates.

sights.name: Vietnam Museum of Ethnology
sights.note: A thorough look at Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups, with a garden of full-size traditional houses, a Bahnar communal hall and a tomb hut to walk through.

sights.name: Vietnamese Women's Museum
sights.note: Four well-curated floors on women's roles in Vietnamese family life, the wars and the economy, with textiles and costumes from ethnic minorities.

sights.name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
sights.note: The granite mausoleum on Ba Đình Square where Ho Chi Minh's embalmed body lies in state; strict dress code, silence, and bags and cameras checked in first.
sights.hours: Mornings only ~7:30–10:30 AM (to ~11:00 AM weekends), Tue–Thu, Sat–Sun; closed Mon & Fri and for an annual maintenance period (usually mid-June to mid-August)

sights.name: Hoan Kiem Lake
sights.note: The tree-lined lake at the heart of the city, with the little Turtle Tower on its islet; locals jog and do tai chi along its shore at dawn.
sights.hours: Open 24 hours; lakeside streets car-free Fri–Sun evenings

sights.name: Ngoc Son Temple
sights.note: A small temple on an islet in Hoàn Kiếm Lake, reached by the red-painted Thê Húc bridge, housing a preserved giant turtle.

sights.name: Hanoi Train Street
sights.note: A narrow lane where the Hanoi–Lào Cai line squeezes between houses and cafés a metre from the rails; police periodically restrict access, so check before going.
sights.hours: Trains pass a few times a day, mostly afternoon and evening; café access varies

sights.name: St. Joseph's Cathedral
sights.note: A soot-darkened neo-Gothic cathedral from 1886, its twin towers fronting a small square full of lemon-tea stalls.
sights.hours: Interior usually open ~8:00–11:00 AM and ~2:00–6:00 PM; Masses daily

sights.name: Imperial Citadel of Thang Long
sights.note: A UNESCO-listed site of the old royal citadel, with the Đoan Môn gate, Kính Thiên palace terrace, wartime command bunkers and excavated foundations.
sights.hours: 8:00 AM–5:00 PM, closed Mon; night tours on selected evenings

sights.name: Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House
sights.note: The simple wooden house beside a carp pond in the Presidential Palace grounds where Ho Chi Minh lived and worked from 1958 to 1969.
sights.hours: ~7:30–11:00 AM & ~2:00–4:00 PM; closed Mon & Fri afternoons

sights.name: One Pillar Pagoda
sights.note: A tiny wooden shrine perched on a single stone pillar in a lotus pond, a symbol of the city rebuilt after it was destroyed in 1954.

sights.name: Tran Quoc Pagoda
sights.note: Hanoi's oldest Buddhist pagoda, with a slender red stupa on a spit of land in West Lake that glows at sunset.

sights.name: Hanoi Opera House
sights.note: A grand 1911 French opera house modelled on the Palais Garnier, still hosting concerts, ballet and the Lune Production shows.
sights.hours: Exterior anytime; open inside for performances and scheduled guided tours

sights.name: Lotte Observation Deck
sights.note: A 65th-floor deck in Lotte Center with 360° views over the city, West Lake and the Red River, plus a glass-floor skywalk.

sights.name: Long Bien Bridge
sights.note: A rusting 1903 cantilever bridge across the Red River, now carrying only trains, scooters and pedestrians; walk out for river views and sunset.

sights.name: Ta Hien Beer Street
sights.note: The Old Quarter's nightlife alley, where locals and travellers crowd onto plastic stools for cheap bia hơi and snacks.

railStations.name: Hanoi Railway Station
railStations.note: Ga Hà Nội on Lê Duẩn, terminus of the North–South Reunification Express to Huế, Đà Nẵng and Ho Chi Minh City; northbound trains to Lào Cai (Sa Pa) and Hải Phòng mostly use the rear Trần Quý Cáp platforms (Ga B). Not on the metro yet; it is 1.5 km west of Hoàn Kiếm Lake.
railStations.hours: Trains by timetable, including overnight sleepers; ticket hall ~6:00 AM–10:00 PM.

airports.name: Noi Bai International Airport
airports.transitNote: No rail link and not on the subway map. Airport express bus 86 (VND 45,000, cash or contactless card) runs from T1 and T2 via Long Biên and the Opera House to Hanoi Railway Station in ~50–60 min; city bus 17 and 90 are cheaper and slower. Taxis and Grab take ~35–50 min to the Old Quarter.
airports.hours: Bus 86 from the airport ~6:40 AM–~10:15 PM (every ~45 min); later arrivals: taxi or Grab.
